extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department chairs, faculty involved in curriculum and graduate program reform, and MER organizers/policy makers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of how university mathematics departments adopt and implement undergraduate and graduate education reforms (curriculum, pedagogy, technology, minority outreach) and the role of MER workshops/networks in facilitating those changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing and faculty ability to teach reform curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments were concerned about their department’s ability to properly staff these courses (reformed calculus requiring more “mathematical maturity” than traditional calculus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns led to extended faculty discussions (e.g., Penn State faculty met bi-monthly for a year before adopting Harvard text). Assessment of staffing includes faculty familiarity with new pedagogy and capacity to teach reformed courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption vs. alternative reforms (Harvard Calculus vs cooperative learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all institutions equate calculus reform with Harvard Calculus; alternatives (e.g., cooperative learning pedagogy) exist and departments may favor different models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reform proposals relative to departmental context, resources, and class size; recognize that adoption may be contested (some departments adopt Harvard, others pursue alternatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class size and resource constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The current large class sizes without any promise of an increase in resources for reducing class size is a primary concern (e.g., Rutgers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether reforms are feasible given class size and resource availability; resource constraints may hinder adoption even when pedagogy is supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and accuracy of mathematics presented
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments were admirably concerned about the quality and accuracy of the mathematics they were presenting to their students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms and materials should be vetted for mathematical correctness and depth; departmental oversight and scholarly review are important safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence of MER workshops and networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Many individual faculty members had attended MER workshops and used this information to try to bring about changes at their own university; MER influenced adoption in some departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure MER's influence by tracking workshop attendance, subsequent local initiatives, and departmental adoptions (examples: UCSB, Penn State, Nebraska).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced presentation in MER workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop presenters were not simply there pushing Harvard calculus; attendees appreciated candor and a balanced view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops should present multiple perspectives, discuss advantages/disadvantages, and avoid appearing to push a single product or viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching excellence (workshop content and departmental policies)
rubrics_metrics.description: MER provides information and resources to improve teaching; workshops include sessions like 'Policies and initiatives for promoting excellence in teaching.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether workshops translate into departmental policies supporting peer evaluation, mentoring, and explicit policies that reward teaching; assess follow-up and continuation (e.g., continued discussions via internet).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for departmental support for individual teaching initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual efforts will only go so far without departmental support; departments wanted to develop understanding for peer evaluation and policies supportive of teaching excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine institutional structures (mentoring, evaluation, workload, rewards) that enable or block individual faculty from sustaining pedagogical innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technology in instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of technology (graphing calculators, mathematical software, instructor use of software in lectures, smart classrooms) is a pedagogical innovation occurring in many departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess depth of integration (demo vs student use), infrastructure (smart classrooms, labs), instructor training, and whether technology supports conceptual understanding or acts as a crutch. Examples: Penn State smart lectern, computer labs, Mathematica/Maple use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student access to and use of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty realized that only having students view the professor’s use of the software was not enough, so they constructed computer laboratories where students can use software with homework problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate opportunities for hands-on student interaction with technology (labs, assignments), funding for student access, and classroom redesign to take advantage of dynamic visualizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative evaluation of technology-based instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics faculty asked a math education faculty member and a graduate student to help implement a formative evaluation for technology use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for formative assessment of learning outcomes and processes when integrating technology; evaluate evidence of learning gains and iterative improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary programs and mathematician involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of interdisciplinary courses/programs (particularly with science and engineering) is a concern; faculty want mathematicians to stay involved in mathematics teaching that occurs in other subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess joint course development, ownership of mathematical content across departments, and mechanisms to keep mathematicians engaged (e.g., curriculum agreements, joint appointments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-time vs broad/vertical mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: A speaker suggested two components: horizontal (wide, broad base of mathematics) and vertical (deep learning when the situation arises), proposing some mathematics be 'delivered on a just-in-time basis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider curricular design that balances breadth and depth and explores modular, just-in-time instructional strategies for applied contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics and conceptualization for multi-university interdisciplinary projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary efforts are often inhibited by logistics; MER hosted a worksession to conceptualize an NSF proposal for an interdisciplinary program across universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate feasibility, administrative coordination, funding models, and MER's facilitation role when planning large cross-institutional projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate education reform responsive to job market
rubrics_metrics.description: Dwindling academic jobs for new Ph.D.’s is driving interest in graduate education reform to make students more marketable (more teaching experience, applied programs, master’s options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess program adjustments (teaching opportunities, teaching-methods courses, applied math tracks, master’s programs, postdoc adjunct roles) aimed at improving employability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate teaching preparation and TA training
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students reported insufficient teaching experience; programs like Washington, Minnesota, and Rutgers’ TA training provide workshops and mentoring for teaching assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate availability and quality of TA training, mentorship during first semester, structured teaching experiences, and recognition of teaching skills in job placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying exams: content relevance and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions were raised about the value and preparation for qualifying exams and whether core courses are simply preparing students for quals rather than important mathematics content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine alignment of qualifying exams with desired learning outcomes, their role in diversity/access, and whether exam content should be revised or rethought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate student professional development and exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops generated ideas like graduate students visiting other MER universities for research talks, semester exchanges, and adjunct post-doctorate positions to increase job prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess support for exchanges, visiting presentations, short-term adjunct opportunities, and institutional mechanisms to facilitate such mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minority participation programs (Treisman-type: Emerging Scholars / Project Excel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs are intended to retain math majors by helping them succeed; presented as honors, selective, with three weekly two-hour study sessions led by a TA assigning creative, real-world problems to small groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate program intensity, selectivity, community-building, hours required, effectiveness for dedicated students, and suitability for scaling or adapting to other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minority-focused workshop models using Harvard Calculus (MAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Math Achievement Program (MAP) used Harvard Calculus and provided intensive recitation/workshop sessions (90 minutes, 3 times/week) in a comfortable dedicated room, limited to 20 students; internal evaluation indicates success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess physical environment, cohort size, curriculum alignment (Harvard Calculus), encouragement vs requirement for participation, and internal evaluation results when judging program efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: K–12 outreach and teacher professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments engage in in-service teacher enhancement, curriculum design projects, and policy work (e.g., Regional Geometry Institute, Tri-County Mathematics Project, South Coast Mathematics Partnership, Teaching Fellow program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate programs for improving teachers’ mathematical content and pedagogical knowledge, sustained follow-up, regional impact, partnership networks, and alignment with state frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridges between mathematics and education departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Bridges exist to varying extents: joint appointments, co-PI relationships on grants, math faculty serving on education dissertation committees, and jointly run teacher-preparation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the depth of collaboration (joint appointments vs occasional cooperation), incentives for cross-department work, political/institutional barriers, and MER’s potential to facilitate such bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building departmental credibility and networks via MER membership
rubrics_metrics.description: By including thirteen departments as founding members, MER gained instant credibility in the department; participants felt less isolated and could reference peer institutions' experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider MER’s role in legitimizing reforms through peer networks, testimony opportunities, and cross-departmental conversations that enable local adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and tenure recognition for educational work
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching is a necessary but not sufficient condition for tenure/promotion; faculty who devote energy to education often slow their research productivity and may be disadvantaged, though rare cases of promotion for educational work exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional reward structures, career impacts for educational engagement, and strategies (MER advocacy, databases of pedagogical work) to raise the prestige and acceptance of educational scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for centralized resources (database) to leverage pedagogy acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: ...there is potential for MER developing an effective database covering several campuses. MER may provide leverage for making math pedagogy more acceptable at research universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess creation and maintenance of shared resources (databases, evidence repositories) that document pedagogical effectiveness and provide leverage in departmental reward conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering minority students in small sections as a retention strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Penn State created small (~30 student) sections where minority students were clustered and led by a highly regarded teacher committed to program goals; initial success led to securing additional resources to teach all calculus in small sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clustering as an approach to create safer participation spaces, foster study groups, and its influence on obtaining institutional support for broader changes (e.g., reduced section sizes).
